concepts.why: Biblical-theological and academic readers: the name is Matthew's 'the essence of the Law and the Prophets', and Mark 12:33 says only that love is 'more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices'. It speaks of love against sacrifice, not of the Law and the Prophets. It belongs in concept 11 (Justice, mercy, and faithfulness) beside Hosea 6:6, with its note unchanged. Mark 12:31 and the Romans 13 verses are close enough to stay.

Reformed, Baptist (including Sabbatarian readers), Catholic and academic readers: Romans 14:5 never says 'Sabbath'. It says 'a certain day'. Whether Paul means the Sabbath is disputed, and Jewish readers of Paul commonly take Romans 14 to concern food and fast days. Setting it under 'Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy' decides in the site's voice that it is about the Sabbath. Colossians 2:16-17 and Hebrews 4:9 name the Sabbath and stay.

Academic reader: the name is 'Wisdom and the commandments'. Deuteronomy 10:12-13 has the fear of the LORD and the commandments but no word of wisdom or understanding, so it shares a theme with the others rather than holding the concept. Psalm 111:10 already carries the fear of the LORD with wisdom. Ecclesiastes 12:13 can stay as the one bridge from a wisdom book to the commandments.

'Christ and the law' is acceptable to all nine as a plain label. It names two things and no relation. It is the texts' own pairing: Romans 10:4 and Galatians 3:24 say 'Christ', and Luke 24:44 has Jesus speaking of the Law of Moses and what is 'written about Me'. A Jewish-aware academic might prefer 'Jesus' for Matthew 5:17-19 and Luke 16:17, but 'Christ' is the New Testament's own word and the label asserts no fulfilment, so I would not change it. Matthew 5:17 'fulfill' appears only inside the note, which is correct. Keep Romans 10:4's note unglossed and keep Romans 3:31 and Matthew 5:18-19 beside it, so the concept does not lean either way.

concepts.name: The law of commandments and decrees
concepts.why: Jewish-aware academic, Reformed, Catholic and Baptist readers: 'Changed, set aside, abolished' states three outcomes as a heading, in the site's voice. Heard together they read as the site's thesis about the Mosaic law, which is exactly where Christians part (Matthew 5:17-19 against Ephesians 2:15; ceremonial against moral law; Israel and the church). Hebrews 8:13 is about 'the first one' (the covenant), and Colossians 2:14 and Ephesians 2:15 are read by many as the decrees dividing Jew from Gentile. A name from the texts' nouns fits every passage: Ephesians 2:15 'the law of commandments and decrees', Colossians 2:14 'the decrees', Hebrews 7:18 'the former commandment', Hebrews 7:12 'the law'. The notes already carry each passage's own verb (changed, set aside, obsolete, abolishing, canceled), so the quoted verbs stay and the heading no longer asserts them.

concepts.name: Justified
concepts.why: Reformed, Catholic, Wesleyan and Lutheran readers: 'Justified before God' puts James 2:21-24 into God's courtroom. James never says 'before God', and whether James speaks of God's verdict or of vindication before others is exactly what these traditions dispute. Romans 4:2 and Galatians 3:11 do use 'before God', but the phrase should not head a concept that also holds James. The plain label 'Justified' is true of every passage here and settles nothing. The notes keep each author's own words, with Paul and James side by side and no ruling between them.

secondary_or_links: Secondary concepts: no change. Each is a verse-level quotation with a plain label, and the Law, Prophets and Gospel citations are shown side by side without saying one fulfils another.

Links: no change. 'Messiah/Christology' is an existing site label and asserts nothing. The closing 'I will give you a new heart' meets the hope rule, with the dark concepts (21, 22, 28) all kept before it. Hebrews 8:10 quotes Jeremiah 31 verbatim. 2 Corinthians 3:3 is only an echo, but it quotes the stone-and-heart contrast and the placement claims nothing beyond the verse, so I leave it.

Concept 6 loses Mark 12:33, which should be added to concept 11 with its note unchanged ('This is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices'), beside Hosea 6:6, Matthew 9:13 and Matthew 12:7. Concept 11 would then hold six passages.
